name: Honda K20C1 2.0 L DOHC VTEC TURBO inline-four (Civic Type R FK8, 2017-2021; US rating 306 hp SAE net, Japan/Europe 320 PS)
induction: turbocharged (single mono-scroll MHI TD04, electrically actuated internal wastegate), direct injection, air-to-air front-mounted intercooler
status_note: Researched by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-17. Definition engines/defs/honda_k20c1.json written 2026-11-17 (Claude Opus 5.5); its notes list what is estimated. Key quotes (bore, stroke, compression, power, boost, firing order) re-read on the source pages the same day.
summary: An almost square (86.0 x 85.9 mm) 2.0 L four firing every 180 degrees into a cylinder head with the exhaust manifold cast in, feeding one small mono-scroll turbo whose electric wastegate is held wide open at light load and closed to spin the turbine up; VTEC switches only the exhaust cam, and both cams are phased by VTC. Full torque (400 N m) arrives at about 2500 rpm and holds to 4500 rpm, power peaks at 6500 and the engine is cut at 7000; testers describe a breathy exhaust roar, an 'air rush' above about 5000 rpm and hissing turbo and valve noises rather than a classic VTEC howl, all leaving through a centre triple outlet whose middle pipe is a resonator that adds sound at low speed and draws air in at mid load to cancel cabin boom.

owner_figures_check.2.0 L turbo inline-four: Confirmed: 'Turbocharged In-Line 4-Cylinder', 1,996 cc (Honda US spec sheet); Japan spec list 'エンジン型式：K 20 C', '水冷直列4気筒横置' (water-cooled inline four, transverse), 1.995 L.
owner_figures_check.306 hp: Confirmed as the US SAE net rating ('306 @ 6,500 rpm', Honda US spec sheet). Japan and Europe rate the same engine 235 kW (320 PS) at 6500 rpm. 306 hp is 228 kW (my arithmetic, 306 x 0.7457); 320 PS is 315.6 hp. The difference is the rating standard and market calibration; no Honda source explains it.
owner_figures_check.22.8 psi boost: Confirmed in the US spec sheet and the powertrain release table, but the same release also says 'a maximum of 23.2 psi of turbocharger boost' in another section; see boost_psi.
owner_figures_check.single-scroll MHI TD04, internal wastega: Confirmed: 'Single-Scroll MHI TD04 with Internal Wastegate' (Honda US spec sheet); the wastegate is electrically actuated (Honda US powertrain release, Honda Japan press information).
owner_figures_check.VTEC on the exhaust cam only: Confirmed by Honda: 'VTECは排気側だけに適用した' (VTEC was applied only to the exhaust side), Honda Japan technology page; also JE Pistons and Hondata.

engine_code.value: K20C1 (Honda Japan prints the type as K20C)
engine_code.note: Honda Japan spec list for the UK-built FK8 sold in Japan (6BA-FK8, 2020-2021): 'エンジン型式 ： K 20 C'. The suffix K20C1 is used by Wikipedia ('2017–2021 Honda Civic Type R (USDM)' in the K20C1 row, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_K_engine), by JE Pistons ('Inside The Honda K20C1 (Type R) Cylinder Head') and by parts fitment listings ('Honda 2.0L/1996CC - 4 Cylinder (K20C1)', kseriesparts.com). No Honda document read uses the '1' suffix. The same engine was in the 2015-2017 European FK2 at 310 PS (Honda's 2015 press information and Honda's K20C technology page); FK2 documents are used below only where labelled.

variant.value: FK8 Civic Type R, 2017-2021: US 306 hp (SAE net) at 6500 rpm and 295 lb-ft from 2500 to 4500 rpm; Japan/Europe 235 kW (320 PS) at 6500 and 400 N m from 2500 to 4500. Engine built in Anna, Ohio; car built in Swindon, UK.
variant.note: US spec sheet: 'Horsepower (SAE net) 306 @ 6,500 rpm', 'Torque (SAE net) 295 lb-ft @ 2,500-4,500 rpm'. Honda Europe release of 7 June 2017 (https://hondanews.eu/eu/en/cars/media/pressreleases/108909/2017-honda-civic-type-r1): 'Peak power output from the optimised and refined 2.0-litre VTEC TURBO engine is 320 PS at 6,500rpm'. Build locations: a search excerpt of a Honda Canada release ('produced exclusively in Honda's Swindon, UK plant with the engine produced in Anna, Ohio'); not opened, so a lead only. Honda says the FK8 gained 10 PS over the FK2 through the exhaust: 'CIVIC TYPE R（FK8）への適用では、排気系の見直しにより最高出力は約7.4kW（10ps）アップの235kW（320ps）を実現した' (Honda K20C technology page). The 2020 facelift added Active Sound Control (PistonHeads); not modelled here.

layout.note: 'エンジン種類・シリンダー数及び配置：水冷直列4気筒横置' (water-cooled inline four, transverse). Aluminium block: 'アルミブロックやエキマニレス構造等の採用により、エンジン全体の軽量化も達成' (aluminium block and a manifold-less head reduce weight), Honda Japan press information, Civic TYPE R, July 2017, page 10 (https://www.honda.co.jp/factbook/auto/CIVIC/201707/20170727_civic-typeR_p09.pdf).

bore_mm.note: US spec sheet: 'Bore and Stroke (mm) 86.0 x 85.9'. Same in the Honda Japan spec list ('内径×行程 ： 86 . 0 mm × 85 . 9 mm'), the Honda Europe release (86.0 x 85.9) and Wikipedia ('86 mm').

stroke_mm.note: '86.0 x 85.9' (US spec sheet); identical in the Japan spec list and the Europe release. Honda Japan calls it a square bore and stroke: '軽量クランクシャフトやスクエアボア×ストロークの採用により軽快なエンジンレスポンスを実現' (press information, July 2017, page 5, https://www.honda.co.jp/factbook/auto/CIVIC/201707/20170727_civic-typeR_p04.pdf).

displacement_cc.note: 'Displacement (cc) 1,996'. The Honda Japan spec list prints '総排気量 ： 1 . 995 L' (Japanese type-approval figures are usually truncated rather than rounded; that is my reading of the 1 cc difference). 86.0 x 86.0 x 85.9 x pi/4 x 4 = 1995.9 cc (my arithmetic).

rod_length_mm.note: Not found in a page I could open. Leads from search excerpts only: Brian Crower ProH2K rods for the FK8 listed as 'Standard Length' at '5.656" / 143.66mm' (turbotechperformance.com and realstreetperformance.com; both refused or rate-limited the fetch), a BoostLine set at 144.00 mm (vividracing.com, 403), and a Skunk2 set at 139.00 mm (a4h-tech.com, 403), which disagrees. Honda describes the stock rods only as hot- then cold-forged 'partially strengthened' rods ('コンロッドの棹部は熱間鍛造に加えて冷間鍛造することで高強度化した部分強化コンロッド', press information page 10). If a value is needed, about 143.7 mm is the better-supported lead; it is not a sourced figure.

compression_ratio.note: 'Compression Ratio 9.8 : 1' (US spec sheet). Same in the Honda Japan spec list ('圧縮比 ： 9.8'), the Honda Europe release and the US powertrain release table.

firing_order.note: Not found in any document naming the K20C1, K20C2 or FK8; this is the K-series family order. Haltech (engine-management maker) 'Honda K Series Engine' article lists firing order '1-3-4-2' for the K20A/K24A family. Factory RSX (K20A3) service data reproduced by workshop-manuals.com: 'Firing Order 1 - 3 - 4 - 2' (https://workshop-manuals.com/acura/rsx/l4-2.0l_(vtec)/engine_cooling_and_exhaust/engine/tune-up_and_engine_performance_checks/firing_order/component_information/specifications/). Honda's own K20C page is consistent with it but does not state the order: '4気筒エンジンは1番と4番シリンダーの排気と、2番と3番シリンダーの排気が干渉するため、レスポンスの低下を招きやすい' (in a four-cylinder engine the exhaust of cylinders 1 and 4 and that of cylinders 2 and 3 interfere, which tends to hurt response), the usual reason for pairing 1+4 and 2+3 in a twin-scroll turbine; that pairing fits 1-3-4-2 (and also 1-2-4-3), my reading. The Syvecs FK2/FK8 plug-in ECU pinout lists the injector drivers in the order 1, 3, 4, 2 (https://www.syvecs.com/downloads/Syvecs_FK2_Kit_Manual.pdf, 'LS1 Injector 1 ... LS3 Injector 3 ... LS5 Injector 4 ... LS12 Injector 2'); treating that as the firing order is my inference. Search excerpts from carscounsel.com and rerev.com (both 403) also give 1-3-4-2 for the K20; one excerpt from motorreviewer.com gave 1-3-2-4 for 'the K-series', which no other source supports. Single bank, so no bank assignment.

cylinder_numbering.note: Which end cylinder 1 is at was not found for the K20C1 [NO CITATION FOUND]. Searches turned up only a generic site saying cylinder 1 is at the timing-chain end on most Honda engines (tpautorepair.net, search excerpt, not opened). The K20C1's cams are chain-driven ('DOHC チェーン駆動', Japan spec list). For sound modelling with an even-firing four the choice does not change the firing intervals.

crank.value: Four-throw crankshaft with 8 counterweights ('semi-counter 8-weight'), lightweight forged steel; flat-plane (pins 1 and 4 together, 2 and 3 together) assumed
crank.note: Honda Japan press information, page 10, figure label: '超軽量セミカウンター8ウエイトクランクシャフト' (ultra-light semi-counter 8-weight crankshaft). US powertrain release (https://hondanews.com/releases/honda-civic-type-r-powertrain): 'a specially developed, super lightweight forged-steel crankshaft is used exclusively in the Civic Type R.' The pin layout is not stated anywhere read; flat-plane is the only layout that gives even 180-degree firing with this order and is my assumption. Wikipedia (uncited): 'K20C1 engines have an offset of 8mm on the crankshaft from the centerline of the bore' (a desaxe offset); not confirmed in a Honda source.

firing_intervals_deg.note: My derivation from the 1-3-4-2 order on a flat-plane four (720 / 4).

valves_per_cylinder.note: '弁機構 ： DOHC チェーン駆動 吸気 2 排気 2' (DOHC, chain drive, 2 intake, 2 exhaust). US spec sheet: '16-Valve DOHC VTEC'. Exhaust valves are sodium-filled: 'the turbo engine utilizes sodium-filled exhaust valves' (US powertrain release); 'ナトリウム封入エキゾーストバルブ' (Japan press information page 11). Rockers: aluminium VTEC rocker arms ('アルミ製VTECロッカーアーム', Japan press information page 10); JE Pistons: 'the springs are now single (not dual) beehive-style units topped by aluminum roller rockers'.

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: Weak (aftermarket): Ferrea F2396P intake valve listed for the K20C1 ('Honda 2.0L/1996CC - 4 Cylinder (K20C1)', 2017-2021 Civic Type R): 'Head Diameter: 35 mm', 'Stem Diameter: 5.48 mm', 'Overall Length: 117.25 mm'. The product name on other retailers includes 'Stock Comp Plus Intake Valve' (ggcracing.com, rate-limited, URL only), and Ferrea also sells a 36 mm '+1mm' version (search excerpt), so 35 mm as the stock size is my reading of those names. No Honda figure found; JE Pistons' head article gives no valve sizes.

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: Weak (aftermarket): Ferrea F2394P exhaust valve for the K20C1: 'Head Diameter: 29 mm', 'Stem Diameter: 5.47 mm', 'Overall Length: 114.75 mm', '28 Degree Taper Flo.Stock size. Super Alloy'. The OEM valve is sodium-filled (Honda); this replacement is not.

intake_lift_mm.note: Not found. Honda publishes no cam data in the sources read; 4 Piston Racing's camshaft test (https://4pistonracing.com/blogs/news/k20c1-camshaft-testing) gives no stock figures. Aftermarket drop-in cams (Kelford 252/260 deg, 9.90/10.40 mm; Skunk2 Ultra Stage 1) were seen only in search excerpts and are not stock.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: Not found, for either the low or the high exhaust lobe.

exhaust_duration_deg.note: Not found. Honda describes the low exhaust lobe as 'narrow opening angle' and the high lobe as 'wide opening angle' (see vtec) but gives no numbers.

vtec.value: Exhaust side only: a narrow-duration low cam and a wide-duration high cam on the exhaust valves; the intake has one profile
vtec.note: Honda K20C technology page (published 13 November 2025): 'K20C型はターボチャージャーで十分な空気をシリンダーに送り込めることから、VTECは排気側だけに適用した' (because the turbo can push enough air into the cylinders, VTEC was applied to the exhaust side only). US powertrain release: VTEC 'changes valve lift, timing and duration of the exhaust valves.' JE Pistons, quoting 4 Piston Racing: 'There is no VTEC on the intake cam, and I wish there was'. Wikipedia: 'The VTEC mechanism is available only on the exhaust valves.' Honda's strategy (Japan press information page 10; same text in the 2015 FK2 press information page 13, https://www.honda.co.jp/factbook/auto/CIVIC_TYPE_R/201510/P13.pdf): at start and idle, minimum overlap; for boost response at low speed, more overlap to maximise scavenging, 'VTECは狭開角カム（ローカム）で排気脈動を制御、低回転域での高トルク・高レスポンスを実現' (VTEC uses the narrow low cam to control exhaust pulsation for low-speed torque and response); for economy at part load, more overlap for internal EGR with 'VTECは高開角カム（ハイカム）'; for full-throttle output, less overlap to cut residual gas, with the high cam to cut pumping loss.

cam_switch_rpm.note: No single switch speed is published; the switch is scheduled by load as well as speed. Hondata (FK2/FK8 tuning notes): 'VTEC is off at idle, on at cruise, off when the turbo is spooling and on at high load.' This matches Honda's description above (low cam while boost builds, high cam at part-load cruise and at full output). Hondata also: 'VTEC is exhaust only and controls the exhaust back pressure, which also affects the turbo.' The rpm at which the high cam returns at full load was not found.

vtc.value: Continuously variable phase on both the intake and the exhaust camshafts (Dual VTC). Typical ranges in the stock calibration per Hondata: intake -25 to +30 deg, exhaust -25 to +20 deg (negative = advance)
vtc.unit: cam deg (Hondata does not say crank or cam degrees)
vtc.note: Hondata: 'A typical intake camshaft range is -25 degrees to +30 degrees,' 'the exhaust camshaft range is -25 degrees to +20 degrees.' 'A negative value indicates advance, a positive value indicates retard, for both intake and exhaust camshafts.' Honda: 'バルブタイミングを連続可変させるVTCは吸排気バルブに採用' (VTC on intake and exhaust valves), Japan press information page 10; Europe release: 'Dual-VTC (Dual-Variable Timing Control)'; US powertrain release: 'The system combines intake and exhaust VTC'. Conflict: the US release's specification table prints '16-Valve DOHC VTEC w/intake VTC' while its text and comparison table say intake and exhaust (Dual); Honda's own Japanese documents say both cams, so Dual is used. Honda's phase maps were not found.

redline_rpm.note: 'Redline 7,000 rpm' (US spec sheet); 'Engine redline – 7,000 rpm' (US powertrain release). Honda K20C page: 'レッドゾーンは7000rpmに設定'.

rev_limiter_rpm.note: Hondata: 'We do not recommend raising the rev limiter from the factory setting of 7000 rpm.' 'The high pressure fuel pump will float and be damaged at 3600rpm (7200 rpm engine speed).' Wikipedia also gives 7000 for both redline and limiter. evo calls it 'a satisfying hard rev-cutout'. JE Pistons quotes 4 Piston Racing: 'The valvetrain starts to float at about 7,300rpm.'

idle_rpm.note: Not found. The car has idle stop ('アイドリングストップ装置', Japan spec list).

peak_power_kw.note: US: 'Horsepower (SAE net) 306 @ 6,500 rpm'; 306 hp x 0.7457 = 228.2 kW (my arithmetic). Japan and Europe: 235 kW (320 PS) at 6500 rpm ('最高出力 ： 235kW［320PS］/6,500rpm', Japan spec list; Europe release). Australian cars were rated 228 kW on 95 RON fuel (CarsGuide: 'Its 228kW output is actually slightly down on overseas numbers, thanks to a retune for 95 RON fuel'). The US value is used because the vehicle block is the US car; the torque curve below is Honda Japan's 235 kW curve.

peak_torque_nm.note: '最大トルク： 400N・m［40.8kgf・m］/2,500rpm - 4,500rpm'. US: '295 lb-ft @ 2,500-4,500 rpm' = 399.97 N m (my arithmetic, x 1.35582), so all markets agree on torque.

peak_torque_rpm.note: A flat plateau from 2500 to 4500 rpm (US, Japan, Europe). Wikipedia's family row gives '2500–4000 rpm', which covers later versions; not used.

torque_curve_nm.note: My reading of Honda's full-load curve 'シビック TYPE R性能曲線図' (new model, red line) on page 11 of the July 2017 Japan press information, rendered at 400 dpi and read against the printed axes (about 1.55 px per N m; reading error about +/-5 N m and +/-50 rpm). The plateau reads 396 against the stated 400, so the readings are about 1 percent low. The curve starts at about 1550 rpm, climbs steeply from 2000 to the plateau at about 2530 rpm (my reading of the corner), holds flat to 4500, then falls steadily. The power curve on the same chart reads about 31 kW at 1400, 56 at 2000, 102 at 2500, 188 at 4500, 236 at 6500 (peak) and 218 at 7000 rpm. This is the 235 kW (320 PS) Japan rating; the US 228 kW car will be about 3 percent lower at the top end (my inference). The previous model (FK2, grey line) is nearly identical below 4500 rpm.

boost_psi.unit: psi (gauge, my inference; Honda does not say)
boost_psi.note: US spec sheet: 'Boost 22.8 psi'. Conflict inside Honda's US powertrain release: 'The Type R's maximum boost pressure, at 22.8 psi, is up from the 16.5 psi found in 1.5-liter Civic turbo models' and elsewhere 'a maximum of 23.2 psi of turbocharger boost'. 22.8 is used because it is in both the spec sheet and the release's table. 22.8 psi = 1.57 bar; 23.2 psi = 1.60 bar (my arithmetic). Gauge rather than absolute is my inference: 22.8 psi absolute would be only about 8 psi of boost, too little for 400 N m from 2.0 L. The speed at which it is reached is not stated; the torque plateau from about 2500 rpm suggests full boost by then (my inference). In the instrument cluster there is a boost gauge ('ブースト圧計', Japan press information page 24).

turbocharger.value: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) TD04, single (mono) scroll, journal bearing; compressor wheel 49.3 mm inducer / 58 mm exducer, cast 17HFI aluminium; turbine wheel 46.5 mm inducer / 41.25 mm exducer, 11 blades
turbocharger.note: Model: 'Single-Scroll MHI TD04 with Internal Wastegate' (US spec sheet). Honda: 'The turbocharged Civic Type R engine employs a small-diameter, low-mass turbine for maximum responsiveness. The mono scroll housing design helps the turbo build boost even at relatively small throttle openings and low rpm' (US press kit overview, https://hondanews.com/en-US/releases/release-acfe25287f7d481b93a0c0c020854e5e-honda-civic-type-r-overview). Why mono-scroll: 'ツインスクロールの場合は2つのスクロールを隔てる隔壁が干渉し、高出力化を阻むことがわかった' (with twin scroll the divider between the scrolls got in the way of high output; Honda K20C page); Japan press information page 10: a mono-scroll turbo gives 'the same response as a twin-scroll turbo of the same size and much more output'. Wheel sizes are aftermarket figures: 27WON (turbo upgrade maker, 11 May 2022, https://perform27won.squarespace.com/blog/27won-civic-type-r-turbocharger-upgrade-design-blog-pt-1): 'The OEM turbocharger found on the 2017-2021 Civic Type R is a TD04 unit designed and produced by MHI', 'journal-bearing', 'The compressor wheel is made of 17HFI cast aluminum ... comes with a 49.3mm compressor wheel inducer and 58mm exducer', 'The OEM turbine wheel has an 11-blade count with a 46.5mm inducer and 41.25mm exducer.' DSPORT (31 January 2025, on MHI's own upgrade, https://dsportmag.com/?p=36670): 'the OEM compressor wheel is a 58mm family wheel with a 49.3mm inducer', 'the OEM turbine wheel features a 46.5mm OD and 41.25mm exducer', and an OEM '66-trim'. Conflict: 49.3 / 58 gives a trim of 72 (my arithmetic), not 66; DSPORT's 'family' size may not be the exducer. Compressor blade count: not found in a page I opened (search excerpts gave '6+6' and '12', conflicting). A/R, MHI part number and maps: not found.

wastegate.value: Internal (integrated) wastegate with an electric actuator mounted on the turbine housing; held fully open at light load (naturally aspirated region), closed to spin the turbine up, then used to set boost with the throttle held wide open
wastegate.note: Honda K20C page: '過給圧制御には、吸気負圧を利用するウェイストゲートではなく、電動アクチュエーターによって制御するため制御自由度が高い電動ウェイストゲートを新開発し採用した' (a newly developed electric wastegate instead of one worked by intake pressure); '軽負荷の自然吸気領域ではウェイストゲートを全開にして排気抵抗を低減' (at light load in the NA region the wastegate is fully open to cut exhaust resistance); '出力要求が高まるとウェイストゲートを閉じて排気をタービンに導き、タービン回転を素早く立ち上げる' (when more output is asked for, the wastegate closes and sends exhaust to the turbine to spin it up quickly); 'インテークマニホールドの内圧が大気圧と同等になった段階でスロットルバルブを全開にし、ウェイストゲートバルブの開き量を変えることで過給圧を制御する' (once manifold pressure reaches atmospheric, the throttle is opened fully and boost is set by the wastegate opening). FK2 press information page 13: 'ターボチャージャーハウジングの強度の高い箇所に電動アクチュエーターを設置' (actuator on a stiff part of the turbo housing). US powertrain release: 'The electrically actuated wastegate allows boost pressure to be precisely controlled.' The ECU logs 'wastegate command and position' (Hondata, https://hondata.mobi/help/flashpro/fk2_fk8.htm). Wastegate flow rejoins the exhaust inside the turbine housing before the catalyst ('Internal Wastegate'; the outlet routing is my inference from 'internal').

bypass_valve.value: Diaphragm-type compressor bypass (recirculating) valve, plastic, mounted on the turbo; whether it is opened electrically or by manifold pressure was not established
bypass_valve.note: Weak (aftermarket descriptions only). Forge recirculating valve listing: it 'bolts directly to the turbo in place of the OEM diaphragm type valve' (the listing says 'Honda Civic Type R 2015', i.e. the FK2; Forge sells the same part for FK2 and FK8 per search excerpts). Turbosmart's direct-fit valve for FK8 and FK2 is 'A direct fit high performance replacement for the factory plastic unit' (https://www.full-race.com/store/turbosmart-honda-civic-type-r-fk8-and-fk2-kompact-supersonic-bov). That it recirculates rather than vents is my inference: the car meters air with a mass-flow meter upstream ('IAT2 is part of the AFM on the intake', Hondata) and Hondata says 'Do not use blow off valves.' The question whether the FK8 has an electronic recirculating bypass valve (as many Honda turbos do) is unresolved; no Honda source mentions the valve at all.

intercooler.value: Air-to-air, high capacity, front-mounted low in the bumper opening
intercooler.note: Europe: 'Charge air is cooled through a high-capacity air-to-air intercooler'. US powertrain release: 'A large low-restriction intercooler is positioned low in the front of the car'. FK2 press information page 14: '大容量インタークーラーは走行風が最大に得られるフロントバンパー開口付近に配置' (large intercooler placed near the front bumper opening where airflow is greatest). Honda's K20C page says the 2022 FL5's intercooler went 'from 9 to 10' rows ('段数を9段から10段に増やして圧力損失の低減を図った'), which implies the FK8's has 9 (my inference). Core size and volume not found.

intake_type.value: turbocharger, front intercooler, single drive-by-wire throttle, plenum intake manifold, high-tumble intake ports; runner geometry not found
intake_type.note: FK2 press information page 14: '高タンブル吸気ポート' (high-tumble intake port) shaped by CAE with the piston crown. US spec sheet: 'Drive-by-Wire Throttle System'. JE Pistons on the intake port: 'The port pinches down really small and has a sharp ledge right before the valve seat'. Throttle diameter, plenum volume and runner dimensions not found.

fuel_system.value: Direct injection, side-mounted injectors on the intake side, maximum 20 MPa, up to three injections per cycle, 7-hole nozzles
fuel_system.note: Honda K20C page: '最大噴射圧20MPaのインジェクターはいわゆるサイドインジェクターで、吸気バルブ側に配置', 'サイクルあたり最大3回の多段噴射'. FK2 press information page 12: '７噴口多段直噴インジェクター' (7-hole multi-stage DI injector). US spec sheet: 'Direct Injection'. Spark plugs are M12: 'The cylinder head includes small M12 sparkplugs, down from the more common M14' (US powertrain release).

header_type.value: exhaust manifold cast into the cylinder head (four ports merging inside the head to one outlet), straight onto the turbine; no separate manifold
header_type.note: Honda K20C page: 'エキゾーストマニホールドはシリンダーヘッドに一体鋳造したうえで、上下から包み込むようにウォータージャケットを配置' (manifold cast integrally with the head, with water jackets wrapping it above and below). US powertrain release: 'With exhaust ports cast directly into the cylinder head, the need for a traditional separate exhaust manifold is eliminated'. Japan press information page 11: the two-piece water jacket lowers exhaust gas temperature by about 100 degrees C ('排ガス温度を約100℃低減'). JE Pistons: 'The K20C1 uses a "headifold," which has internal exhaust runners'. The internal runner lengths and merge layout were not found; the runners are very short compared with a tubular header (my inference from the head-integrated design), so little pulse tuning from the manifold is expected.

exhaust_notes.value: Close-coupled two-bed catalyst under the head; straight exhaust run through the floor tunnel; centre-mounted silencer with a triple outlet: two large main pipes either side carry the flow, and a smaller centre tailpipe fed from a resonator adds sound at low speed and goes to negative pressure at mid load and higher speed, drawing in air and cancelling cabin boom
exhaust_notes.note: Japan press information page 11: 'トリプルエキゾーストシステムは、左右をメインパイプとし、中央の1本は低回転では走り出しの迫力あるサウンド、高回転では負圧効果により不快なこもり音低減に効果を発揮' (main pipes left and right; the centre one gives a powerful pull-away sound at low speed and, by a negative-pressure effect at high speed, reduces unpleasant boom). Diagram labels: 'レゾネーター 走り出しのサウンドの迫力を向上' (resonator: stronger pull-away sound); 'メインパイプ 排気流量を増加させ高出力化' (main pipes: more flow, more power); 'センターテールパイプ 低回転域では左右メインパイプとのトータルの開口面積を増やして音圧を向上。高回転域では負圧効果で不快なこもり音を低減' (centre tailpipe: at low speed adds to the total outlet area with the main pipes, raising sound pressure; at high speed the negative-pressure effect reduces boom); 'ストレート化により排気効率を向上' (straightened layout improves efficiency); the silencer sits at the car's centre to reduce yaw inertia. Europe release: 'at mid-load engine speed, the pressure in the centre tailpipe becomes negative, sucking in ambient air', 'This improves NVH characteristics by eliminating the exhaust booming sound', and 'The flow rate through the exhaust has improved by 10% compared to the previous Type R'. Assistant project leader Hideki Kakinuma (CarThrottle): 'At low RPM exhaust gas is streaming out of all three pipes in order to create a very dynamic, 'roaring' sound', 'At mid and high RPM, the middle pipe creates a certain negative pressure, which reduces the booming noise in the cabin.' US powertrain release: 'The center outlet is a key factor in the sound of the exhaust note in the Type R interior.' Honda K20C page: 'FK8はフロアトンネルを一直線に通す排気レイアウトとしたことで排気効率が向上し' (the FK8's exhaust runs straight through the floor tunnel, improving exhaust efficiency). Catalyst: '■ シリンダーヘッド直下2ベッドキャタライザー' (two-bed catalyst directly below the head; FK2 press information page 12, https://www.honda.co.jp/factbook/auto/CIVIC_TYPE_R/201510/P12.pdf). There is no mechanical exhaust valve in any FK8 document read. 2020 facelift: Active Sound Control (speaker augmentation in the cabin) added (PistonHeads).

knock_and_cooling.value: two-piece water jacket around the in-head exhaust ports, pistons with cooling channels, sodium-filled exhaust valves
knock_and_cooling.note: '2ピースウォータージャケット・シリンダーヘッド、クーリングチャンネル付きピストン、ナトリウム封入エキゾーストバルブを採用しています' (page 11). Hondata: 'It is best to avoid any knock events as they will reduce engine power for a short period each time.'

sound_notes.value: Breathy exhaust roar; an 'air rush' above about 5000 rpm; audible turbo whoosh and valve hiss on lift-off; some testers found the engine note dull or too quiet; a little lag below about 3000-3500 rpm, then torque arrives hard
sound_notes.note: evo (used FK8 review, 11 February 2025, John Barker, Ian Eveleigh, Adam Towler): 'a breathy exhaust roar similar to that of an old Mégane RS'; 'The engine itself isn't totally free of lag – catch it off-guard and it can take some time to wake up'. PistonHeads (Tony Middlehurst, 19 September 2021, https://www.pistonheads.com/news/ph-buying-guides/honda-civic-type-r-fk8-ph-used-buying-guide/44704): 'There was an 'air rush' effect from around 5,000rpm'. CarsGuide (Tim Robson, 16 October 2017, Australian 228 kW car, https://www.carsguide.com.au/car-reviews/honda-civic-type-r-59599): 'The engine can be caught off boost under 3500rpm at times', 'that torque piles in hot and strong right around 3000rpm', 'It could also stand to be a bit more overt with its exhaust noise.' Motor1 (9 March 2017, https://www.motor1.com/reviews/138654/2017-honda-civic-type-r/; this test is of the UK 310 hp car, i.e. the FK2 with the same K20C1 but a different exhaust): 'The turbo lag and loud, hissing theatrics from the wastegate are addictive', 'the turbocharger's whooshing boost', and the engine noise 'is characterless, monotonous and droning'. Whether the hiss Motor1 attributes to the wastegate is in fact the bypass valve is not established. No tester describes a VTEC changeover sound on the stock engine; 4 Piston Racing says an aftermarket cam gives a 'much more audible crack of VTEC' than the stock cams.

missing: firing order from a document naming the K20C1/FK8 (K-series family order 1-3-4-2 used, consistent with Honda's 1+4 / 2+3 exhaust pairing statement)
rod length from any page I could open (aftermarket leads 143.66-144 mm, one outlier at 139 mm)
cam lift, duration and valve timing for the intake cam and both exhaust lobes; the speed at which VTEC changes at full load; Honda's VTC phase maps (Hondata's typical ranges only)
speed at which full boost is reached; whether Honda's 22.8 psi is gauge (assumed) and which of 22.8 and 23.2 psi is right
turbo: MHI part number, A/R, compressor blade count, compressor and turbine maps, shaft inertia; the trim conflict (66 against 72 from the wheel sizes)
bypass (recirculation) valve actuation (electric or pneumatic) and its routing from a Honda source
intake: throttle diameter, plenum volume, runner lengths; intercooler core size and volume
exhaust: in-head runner lengths and merge layout, downpipe and pipe diameters, resonator volume, silencer layout
a US 0-60 mph figure from Honda (Car and Driver's 4.9 s seen only in a search excerpt; the site blocks automated reading)
Honda's statement of the rating standards behind 306 hp (US) against 320 PS (Japan/Europe)

sources.what: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) official 2017 Civic Type R specifications page: turbo model (Single-Scroll MHI TD04 with Internal Wastegate), 22.8 psi, 1,996 cc, 86.0 x 85.9, 9.8:1, 306 hp at 6500, 295 lb-ft at 2500-4500, 7,000 rpm redline, direct injection, gear ratios, final drive, curb weight, tyres, exhaust. Manufacturer document.

Honda US press kit, '2017 Honda Civic Type R - Powertrain' (14 June 2017): electric wastegate, 22.8 and 23.2 psi, intercooler, i-VTEC with intake and exhaust VTC and exhaust VTEC, sodium-filled exhaust valves, exhaust ports cast into the head, M12 plugs, forged crank and rods, triple outlet, spec and comparison tables. Manufacturer document.

Honda US press kit overview (2017): low-mass turbine, mono-scroll housing, centre outlet and sound, 'track top speed of approximately 170 mph'. Manufacturer document; only the first 100,000 characters were read.

Honda Motor Europe press release '2017 Honda Civic Type R' (7 June 2017): 320 PS at 6500, 400 Nm at 2500-4500, electric wastegate, VTEC and Dual-VTC, air-to-air intercooler, triple exhaust with negative pressure in the centre pipe at mid load, 10% more exhaust flow, gear ratios, 1,380 kg, 245/30 R20, 272 km/h, 0-100 km/h 5.7 s. Manufacturer document, figures marked preliminary.

Honda Japan press information (factbook), CIVIC TYPE R, July 2017, pages 4-5 technology digest: square bore and stroke, electric-wastegate turbo, straight exhaust pipe, +10 PS over the previous model. Manufacturer document (PDF read by text extraction).

Same press information, page 10 (powertrain): exhaust-side VTEC and its low/high cam strategy, VTC on intake and exhaust, mono-scroll turbo with electric wastegate, aluminium VTEC rockers, partially strengthened rods, light pistons, semi-counter 8-weight crank, aluminium block, manifold-less head.

Same press information, page 11 (powertrain): two-piece water jacket, cooling-channel pistons, sodium-filled exhaust valves, triple exhaust with resonator, main pipes and centre tailpipe, and the full-load power and torque curve (235 kW / 400 N m) read for torque_curve_nm.

Same press information, printed page 12: lightweight single-mass flywheel, lower final drive, rev-match system. (File names run one behind the printed page numbers: _p09 is page 10, _p10 is page 11, _p11 is page 12.)

Honda Japan spec list for the UK-built CIVIC TYPE R sold in Japan (6BA-FK8, 2020-2021): engine type K20C, 1.995 L, 86.0 x 85.9 mm, 9.8, DOHC chain drive 2+2 valves, 235 kW / 6500, 400 N m / 2500-4500, PGM-FI, FF, gear ratios, final drive 4.111, 1,390 kg, 245/30ZR20 90Y. Type-approval figures.

Honda Japan press information, CIVIC TYPE R (FK2), October 2015, page 12: K20C main technologies (manifold-less head, exhaust VTEC, intake and exhaust VTC, electric wastegate, air-cooled intercooler, 7-hole DI injector, two-bed catalyst directly below the head, semi-counter 8-weight crank). Same engine family, previous car; used where labelled.

Same FK2 press information, page 13: VTC and VTEC control strategy, mono-scroll turbo with electric wastegate, actuator on the turbine housing, wastegate control (throttle fixed wide open, boost set by the wastegate).
Same FK2 press information, page 14: high-tumble ports, multi-stage direct injection, large intercooler near the front bumper opening, cooling measures.

Honda Motor Co. technology history page 'K20C型 CIVIC TYPE R ... VTEC TURBO' (13 November 2025): why mono-scroll, exhaust-only VTEC, Dual VTC, electric wastegate operation, exhaust manifold cast into the head, 20 MPa side injectors, FK8 exhaust revision to 320 PS, FL5 intercooler rows. Manufacturer document.

JE Pistons, 'Inside The Honda K20C1 (Type R) Cylinder Head With 4 Piston Racing' (Evan Perkins, 20 March 2018): VTEC on the exhaust side only, headifold, intake port ledge, beehive springs and aluminium roller rockers, valve float at about 7,300 rpm. Specialist (piston maker) article quoting an engine builder.

Hondata FlashPro 'Tuning Notes' for the FK2 and FK8 Civic Type R (Bosch ECU): factory rev limit 7000, fuel pump limit, VTEC exhaust only and its schedule, typical VTC ranges, AFM and IAT locations, no blow-off valves. Specialist reference from the main Honda ECU tuner.
Hondata FlashPro page 'Civic Type R 2017-2021': logged channels including wastegate command and position, VTEC, knock retard.
Haltech (engine-management maker) knowledge-base article 'Honda K Series Engine': firing order 1-3-4-2 for the K20A/K24A family. Specialist reference; does not name the K20C.
Third-party reproduction of 2002 Acura RSX (K20A3) factory service data: firing order 1-3-4-2. Same engine family, not the K20C.
Syvecs (engine-management maker) plug-in ECU kit manual for the Type R FK2/FK8: OEM electric wastegate controllable, wastegate position input, VTEC output, injector driver list. Specialist document.
Wikipedia, Honda K engine: K20C1 row (9.8:1, 306-315 hp at 6500, redline and limiter 7000, VTEC on exhaust only, 8 mm crank offset). Mostly uncited; cross-check only.
27WON (aftermarket turbo maker) design blog, 11 May 2022: stock MHI TD04 description and compressor and turbine wheel sizes. Specialist, not Honda or MHI.
DSPORT magazine, 'Bad-Ass Bolt-On' (Michael Ferrara, 31 January 2025) on MHI's own upgrade turbo for the Type R: OEM compressor and turbine wheel sizes and trim.
Forge recirculating valve listing (bar-tek): the OEM valve is a diaphragm type bolted to the turbo. Aftermarket; weak.
Turbosmart Kompact valve listing (Full-Race): replaces 'the factory plastic unit' on the FK8 and FK2. Aftermarket; weak.
Ferrea F2396P intake valve listing for the K20C1 (35 mm head). Aftermarket fitment data; weak.
Ferrea F2394P exhaust valve listing for the K20C1 (29 mm head, 'Stock size'). Aftermarket fitment data; weak.
4 Piston Racing, 'K20C1 Camshaft Testing' (22 June 2021): no stock cam data; stock baseline pull to 6800 rpm; aftermarket cam gives a more audible VTEC changeover.
CarThrottle (Matt Robinson, originally 2017): interview with assistant project leader Hideki Kakinuma on the three tailpipes.
evo, 'Used Honda Civic Type R (FK8, 2017-2022) review' (11 February 2025): exhaust sound, lag, hard rev cut, 0-62 and top speed. Road test.
PistonHeads, 'Honda Civic Type R (FK8) PH Used Buying Guide' (Tony Middlehurst, 19 September 2021): 'air rush' above 5000 rpm, triple exhaust, Active Sound Control from 2020. Road-test based guide.
CarsGuide (Tim Robson, 16 October 2017), Australian FK8: off boost below 3500 rpm, torque near 3000, exhaust too quiet, 228 kW on 95 RON. Road test.
Motor1 review (9 March 2017) of the UK 310 hp car (FK2, same K20C1): turbo lag, wastegate hiss, droning engine note. Road test of the previous car; used only as labelled.

vehicle.name: Honda Civic Type R (FK8, 2017, US spec Touring, 6-speed manual)

curb_kg.note: US curb weight 'Curb Weight (lbs.) 3,117'; 3,117 x 0.45359 = 1413.9 kg (my arithmetic). Weight distribution '61.8% / 38.2%' front/rear. Europe: 'Curb weight (kg) 1,380' (Honda Europe release; standard not stated). Japan: '車両重量 ： 1 , 390 kg' (2020-2021 spec list).

gear_count.note: '6-Speed Manual Transmission (6MT) with Adjustable Automatic Rev-Matching'.

gears.note: '1st: 3.625, 2nd: 2.115, 3rd: 1.529, 4th: 1.125, 5th: 0.911, 6th: 0.735, Reverse: 3.758'. Europe and Japan print 6th 0.734 and reverse 3.757 (rounding).

final_drive.note: 'Final Drive Ratio: 4.111'. Same in Europe and Japan. Lightweight single-mass flywheel and helical limited-slip differential.

tyre.note: '245/30ZR20 90Y', 'Maximum-Performance Summer Tires', on '20 x 8.5 Aluminum Alloy' wheels. Europe: '245/30 R20 – Continental SportContact6'.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from 245/30 R20: 254 mm rim radius + 0.30 x 245 = 73.5 mm sidewall = 327.5 mm. Unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius.

driven.note: '駆動方式 ： FF' (front engine, front-wheel drive). US: 'Helical Limited-Slip Differential' at the front ('a helical limited-slip front differential is standard', US powertrain release).

top_speed_kmh.note: Europe: 'will go on to a top speed of 272km/h (169mph)'. Honda US gives only 'a track top speed of approximately 170 mph' (US press kit overview), about 274 km/h (my arithmetic). evo: 'the Type R can manage 169mph flat out'.

zero_to_100_kmh_s.note: Europe: 'covers the 0-100km/h (0-62 mph) sprint in just 5.7 seconds'. Conflict: Honda's Swiss French release gives 5.8 s (search excerpt, not opened) and evo's data table lists 5.8 s for the standard car and 5.7 s for the Limited Edition. No Honda US 0-60 mph figure was found; Car and Driver's instrumented 4.9 s 0-60 was seen only quoted in a search excerpt (caranddriver.com blocks automated reading), and Gear Patrol prints '0-60: 5 seconds (est.)'.
